sentences.text: James VI and I -LRB- 19 June 1566 -- 27 March 1625 -RRB- was King of Scotland as James VI from 24 July 1567 and King of England and Ireland as James I from the union of the Scottish and English crowns on 24 March 1603 until his death .	King of Scotland	List of Scottish monarchs	King of England	List of English monarchs	Ireland	Monarchy of Ireland	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	England	Kingdom of England	union of the Scottish and English crowns	Union of the Crowns

The kingdoms of Scotland and England were individual sovereign states , with their own parliaments , judiciary , and laws , though both were ruled by James in personal union .	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	England	Kingdom of England	personal union	personal union

James was the son of Mary , Queen of Scots , and a great-great-grandson of Henry VII , King of England and Lord of Ireland , positioning him to eventually accede to all three thrones .	King of England	List of English monarchs	Ireland	Monarchy of Ireland	England	Kingdom of England
James succeeded to the Scottish throne at the age of thirteen months , after his mother Mary was compelled to abdicate in his favour .	abdicate	abdicate
Four different regents governed during his minority , which ended officially in 1578 , though he did not gain full control of his government until 1583 .

In 1603 , he succeeded the last Tudor monarch of England and Ireland , Elizabeth I , who died without issue .	Ireland	Monarchy of Ireland	Elizabeth I	Elizabeth I	England	Kingdom of England	Tudor	Tudor dynasty
He continued to reign in all three kingdoms for 22 years , a period known after him as the Jacobean era , until his death in 1625 at the age of 58 .	Jacobean era	Jacobean era

After the Union of the Crowns , he based himself in England -LRB- the largest of the three realms -RRB- from 1603 , only returning to Scotland once in 1617 , and styled himself `` King of Great Britain and Ireland '' .	Ireland	Monarchy of Ireland	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	England	Kingdom of England	styled	style (manner of address)	King of Great Britain and Ireland	King of Great Britain and Ireland
He was a major advocate of a single parliament for England and Scotland .	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	England	Kingdom of England

In his reign , the Plantation of Ulster and British colonization of the Americas began .	Plantation of Ulster	Plantation of Ulster	British colonization of the Americas	British colonization of the Americas

At 57 years and 246 days , James 's reign in Scotland was longer than those of any of his predecessors .	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	longer than those of any of his predecessors	List of monarchs in Britain by length of reign#Scotland

He achieved most of his aims in Scotland but faced great difficulties in England , including the Gunpowder Plot in 1605 and repeated conflicts with the English Parliament .	Scotland	Kingdom of Scotland	England	Kingdom of England	Gunpowder Plot	Gunpowder Plot	English Parliament	English Parliament

Under James , the `` Golden Age '' of Elizabethan literature and drama continued , with writers such as William Shakespeare , John Donne , Ben Jonson , and Sir Francis Bacon contributing to a flourishing literary culture .	Elizabethan literature	Elizabethan literature	William Shakespeare	William Shakespeare	John Donne	John Donne	Ben Jonson	Ben Jonson	Francis Bacon	Francis Bacon

James himself was a talented scholar , the author of works such as Daemonologie -LRB- 1597 -RRB- , The True Law of Free Monarchies -LRB- 1598 -RRB- , and Basilikon Doron -LRB- 1599 -RRB- .	Daemonologie	Daemonologie	The True Law of Free Monarchies	The True Law of Free Monarchies	Basilikon Doron	Basilikon Doron
He sponsored the translation of the Bible that would later be named after him : the Authorised King James Version .	Authorised King James Version	Authorised King James Version

Sir Anthony Weldon claimed that James had been termed `` the wisest fool in Christendom '' , an epithet associated with his character ever since .	Anthony Weldon	Anthony Weldon	Christendom	Christianity
Since the latter half of the 20th century , historians have tended to revise James 's reputation and treat him as a serious and thoughtful monarch .
